question: Does the actually chosen protected set from an eligible mixed layer call recur in that policy's next actual call of the same layer?
evidence_type: STRUCTURAL / retrospective observation of NATIVE_SERVING policy-specific traces

formulas.protected_reuse: |P intersect U| / |P|; aggregate ratio sums numerator and denominator over paired eligible layer calls; zero denominator => null
formulas.unprotected_reuse: |Q intersect U| / |Q| with the same weighting
formulas.next_missing: M = U minus C; previous-final continuity C==F checked, not assumed
formulas.next_active_accounting: |U| = |P intersect U| + |Q intersect U| + |M| when P subset F and C==F
formulas.missing_decomposition: M = (M intersect previous active union) disjoint-union (M minus previous active union)
formulas.boundary: Old requests come from event.before.old_output_tokens; alive at call start iff any old completion_s exceeds that actual engine call start_s.

scopes: Only previous eligible mixed calls; applied and no-cross-group-protection calls both retained, with previous_applied counts.
Next means adjacent measured actual call of the same layer within the same episode, not next eligible call; engine calls joined via recorded scheduler-step intervals.
No-next and unavailable pairs are retained and excluded from reuse-rate denominators; no cross-episode pairing.
Counts are layer-call expert occurrences, not distinct experts across layers, requests, or independent statistical samples.
Both repeats per mode share the same three input documents. Repeat results remain separate; no pooled significance or independent-document claim.
none has no chosen protection: protected rate is null, and its unprotected set is its full final resident set.
Each policy supplies its own future routes/cache. Protected-vs-unprotected association is not randomized and is not a fixed-trace counterfactual or causal byte saving.
Unprotected final residents are a selected survivor set. Expert frequency, reuse within a request, grouping, and future batch/route changes can confound comparisons.
No timing, throughput, or existing whole-episode traffic metric was recomputed. No ensure-touch hit statistic is used.
Per-row routes are not in raw; eligibility/decode expert fields are inherited from recorded runtime metadata.
